Watts made this hymn from Psalm 84, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1How lovely is Your dwelling place, O LORD of Hosts! 2My soul longs, even faints, for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh cry out for the living God. 3Even the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she places her young near Your altars, O LORD of Hosts, my King and my God. 4How blessed are those who dwell in Your house! They are ever praising You. Selah … 8 more verses PSALM 84 · ITS FIRST VERSES · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 84
The sparrow, for her young, With pleasure seeks her nest; And wandering swallows long To find their wonted rest: My spirit faints With equal zeal To rise and dwell Among thy saints. STANZA II
